correctness.rationale: For real C([0,1]) the atomic positive/negative parts of mu have disjoint support and mass 1/2, hence ||mu||=1 and every projection onto ker mu is I-mu tensor h with mu(h)=1. Rank-one Daugavet equality (also verifiable by dense nonsupport test points) gives norm 1+||h||inf. The Lipschitz and amplitude constraints bound |mu(h)| by Phi_L(t)=sum w_m min(t,L/(2m^beta)); the clipped affine ramp h(x)=min(t,-t+Lx) attains every term, establishing exact feasibility L>=2/B and the unique minimum t_L including L=Lc. For s=(L/2)^(1/beta), the exact geometric tail eta(s), uniform Taylor remainder and bounded piecewise derivative imply t_L-1=beta*q^N/N*(1/(1-q)-r)+O(q^N/N^2), N=floor(s), r=s-N. Extremizing the continuous periodic profile gives liminf beta/(1-q) and limsup beta*exp((-log q)/(1-q)-1)/(-log q); both phases are realized. Independently solved finite scalar roots for q=1/2,beta=1 and q=.3,beta=2 with expected phase approach; read provided decimal code but did not treat its finite checks as proof.
residual_risks: The phase expansion is uniform only for fixed q in (0,1) and beta>0, not in degenerating parameter limits.
Projection norms rely on real C([0,1]) and the specified exact atomic functional.
